scores.evidence: Hybrid search: pgvector (HNSW) plus Postgres full-text, merged with reciprocal rank fusion. Then a reranker
scores.rationale: Mechanisms (RRF, HNSW, SSE, ZDR agreements, LLM-judge calibration, pinned embedding versions with stored raw text) are described accurately with real limits stated; only trivial imprecision like upserts keyed on content_hash.

scores.evidence: A chat widget that answers customer questions using only the published help-center articles. Every answer cites the article it came from.
scores.rationale: Solves exactly the stated problem, resolves ambiguities (account data, languages, channels) with explicit, justified deferrals and pull-forward triggers, and is clearly buildable by a small team.

scores.evidence: Fix the response format... The widget, logs, evals, handoff and feedback all depend on it.
scores.rationale: One service plus one loader with clear data ownership, a shared response contract honored by every downstream consumer, and consistency choices (15-min lag, deletion exception) applied uniformly; the one guardrail-ordering tension is explicitly acknowledged and bounded.

scores.evidence: Runs in CI on every PR. Faithfulness is graded by an LLM judge, calibrated against 50 answers graded by people.
scores.rationale: A ticket-derived eval set is built before retrieval or generation work, every phase has measurable exit checks (recall@5 ≥ 0.85, faithfulness ≥ 0.95, injection suite 0 behavior changes), and validation continues post-launch via staged rollout auto-stops and the Phase 6 loop.

scores.evidence: Stack assumptions (please confirm): help center on Zendesk Guide... If your stack is different, change the connectors.
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit and flagged for confirmation, every key decision has a stated revisit trigger describing what changes if the assumption fails, and numeric budgets are presented as chosen caps rather than invented facts.

scores.evidence: When a load is forced to fail, chat keeps serving the last good index... switch-over refused if document count drops > 10%
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures—withdrawn-policy staleness, hallucinated citations, injection via indexed docs, cost attacks, duplicate loads, ticket-API outage with queued retry, session-store loss, parse-failure repair—each with concrete detection and recovery.

scores.evidence: OTel spans, metrics for latency/error/tokens/cost, Langfuse, dashboard plus one alert
scores.rationale: Deployment, rollback, index-version switch-over, kill switch, and domain-meaningful signals are concrete and sized to a small team, but incident ownership and on-call response are never explicitly assigned.

scores.evidence: If it comes within 5 points of our targets at lower total cost, buy it.
scores.rationale: Inference as the dominant driver is controlled (token caps, per-session $0.25, routing, rate limits, spend alert) and the build-vs-buy trade-off is gated, but there is no order-of-magnitude estimate of expected run spend or engineering cost.

scores.evidence: Database schema. This is the widest change: altering it later forces a full re-index.
scores.rationale: Hard-to-reverse choices (schema, embedding version, vendor coupling) get early scrutiny with explicit exit paths—stored raw text for re-embedding, a model wrapper for switching, index versioning, and a buy-out gate—while reversible choices are decided quickly with revisit triggers.

scores.evidence: One service (FastAPI) plus one scheduled loading job, in one repo, sharing one Postgres.
scores.rationale: Simplest workable design (monolith, pgvector, no agent loop, no fine-tuning) with every added element justified by a target, and ten speculative features explicitly deferred behind measurable pull-forward triggers.

scores.evidence: Depends on: Phase 2 search meeting its recall target. Otherwise the answer evals would mostly measure search failures.
scores.rationale: A team could start immediately: a concrete Phase 0 slice, dependency-justified ordering, specific schemas, thresholds and exit checks per phase, and stated adaptation paths (lower threshold, buy instead of build) if results disappoint.

checklist.evidence: Full sync plus webhook updates... Records deletions when articles are unpublished or removed... An unpublished article disappears from results within 15 min.
Split on H2/H3 headings into chunks of 300–500 tokens... documents(doc_id, url, title, locale, visibility, product_area, cms_updated_at, content_hash, status)
150–300 real questions taken from the last 90 days of tickets and help-center searches... Runs in CI on every PR.
Answer only when the bot can cite a retrieved chunk. Otherwise it says it can't answer and hands off.
The bot never answers refunds, billing disputes, legal, security incidents... create a ticket in Zendesk Support... with the transcript, the citations and the handoff reason.
User text and retrieved docs are treated as data... v1 has no tools, so there is nothing to hijack.
Index only published articles marked public... only after logged-in sessions, per-user access filters and a data-protection review are in place.
Personal data in user text is removed before logging. Transcripts are kept for 30 days... zero-data-retention agreement.
Answers that use account data (order status, billing lookups through tools)... Deferred... No customer account data reaches the model.
Weekly content-gap report for the docs team... Resolution/deflection rate, CSAT, content-gap clusters... Agents tag "bot was wrong" or "doc missing".
at most 8k input tokens... Per session: 20 turns or $0.25... first token in under 2.5 s... rate limits per IP and per session.

traps.evidence: The core rule: the bot cites a source or it doesn't answer.
Index only published articles marked public... per-user access filters in search... Deferred, see §7.
Never fine-tune to teach facts: facts change, and the index updates in minutes.
CI posts a baseline eval report on every PR.
No agent loop and no multiple agents... Training a custom reranker. Pull forward when recall stalls below target.

note: An exemplary, proportionate RAG plan—grounding, eval-first sequencing, deletion propagation and explicit reversibility—weakened only by missing incident ownership and no grounded run-cost estimate.
